neighbours.label: quick informal making or producing (cook up, whip up, whip out, bake a), as against eating, buying or other non-making verbs with the same object
fire: After the game the boys cooked up a big pot of chilli.
My mother can whip up a birthday cake in under an hour.
We cooked up a plan to surprise our teacher.
He whipped up a batch of pancakes for the whole camp.
When the guests arrived early, she whipped out a tray of snacks.
The students cooked up a simple soup with garden vegetables.
Grandpa whipped up a quick sauce from leftover tomatoes.
On rainy days we bake a loaf of bread together.
